cands.name: Eliott Rodriguez
cands.bio: Democratic nominee in FL-27. Former Miami TV news anchor: WFOR CBS Miami 1999-Dec 2025, earlier WPLG and WTVJ. Three Emmys; moderated the 2014 Scott-Crist 'Fangate' debate. Has never held public office.
cands.local_ties: Born in New York to Cuban immigrants; family moved to Miami when he was 12; Miami Dade College and University of Miami graduate. Campaign office in Miami.

record.text: Journalist since 1978 (Miami News), TV anchor for four decades; covered the Mariel boatlift, Hurricane Andrew and the Surfside collapse. No elected office.
Platform: housing supply and workforce housing, insurance stability, restoring ACA subsidies, defend Social Security and Medicare, oppose 'the politics of cruelty toward immigrants.'

endorsements.text: Per Wikipedia's FL-27 section: DCCC Red to Blue, Miami-Dade Mayor Daniella Levine Cava, Miami Mayor Eileen Higgins, Democratic Majority for Israel, J Street, Jewish Democratic Council of America, MoveOn.

cands.gaps: No clear portrait URL (site shows only a family photo and logo) so photo omitted. Funding and outside spending not found. Wikipedia noted Cook Political moved the seat from Safe to Likely Republican.

cands.name: Maria Elvira Salazar
cands.bio: Republican; U.S. Rep. since 2021 (FL-27). Longtime Spanish-language TV journalist (Telemundo, Univision, Mega TV); University of Miami and Harvard Kennedy School graduate. Republican assistant whip. No prior elected office before Congress.
cands.local_ties: Born in Little Havana to Cuban exile parents (Nov 1, 1961).

record.text: Sponsor of the DIGNIDAD Act, a comprehensive immigration bill with work authorization and a legal-status path for up to 12 million people; critics such as FAIR call it amnesty.
Chaired the Foreign Affairs Western Hemisphere subcommittee (118th Congress); Crucial Communism Teaching Act, which she introduced, passed the House in Dec 2024.
Sept 2026: criticized Trump's immigration enforcement in a campaign ad; Trump then attacked her publicly (NYT/Politico per Wikipedia).

controversies.text: Business Insider reported in June 2022 that she appeared to have failed to properly disclose a Cano Health stock exchange, potentially violating the STOCK Act. No finding found.
Voted for the Epstein Files Transparency Act on Nov 18, 2025 after previously calling the matter a 'Democratic Hoax'; Wikipedia says she changed course after a directive from Trump.

foreign_ties.text: Endorsed in Oct 2026 by foreign leaders Javier Milei (Argentina), Abelardo de la Espriella (Colombia) and Maria Corina Machado (Venezuelan opposition), which the Washington Post reported sparked 'interference' claims (as listed on Wikipedia's FL-27 page; WaPo article not opened).

endorsements.text: Wikipedia's FL-27 section lists Trump's endorsement as rescinded after the Aug primary (citing Politico, Sept 26, 2026; I could not open it). Other listed backers: Miami-Dade Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz, Florida FOP District 6, Log Cabin Republicans, AIPAC, NFIB, U.S. Chamber of Commerce, Maggie's List, six local mayors.

cands.gaps: No donor or super PAC data found for FL-27. Trump endorsement status relies on Wikipedia's description (primary article not opened). Campaign social accounts not verified.
